To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transfer function coefficients for heat transfers in concrete bricks are obtained by combining numerical and experimental methods.

(1) the TFCs can be generated using a numerical procedure that is simple and fast, (2) the TFC model can be used to predict heat fluxes at any surface of the brick with high accuracy, (3) the TFC can be used to determine the temperature distribution in the brick with high precision and, (4) the TFC is a useful tool for design and performance assessment of hollow concrete bricks.
we developed a numerical procedure that allows the prediction of the coupled heat transfer in hollow concrete bricks in realistic time varying situations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the dynamic thermal properties of hollow concrete bricks, a problem of great importance for the design of energy efficient buildings.
the determination of transfer function coefficients for time-varying coupled heat transfers in hollow concrete bricks.
the development of a numerical procedure for the determination of transfer function coefficients of time-varying coupled heat transfers in hollow concrete bricks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the empirical TFCs are an excellent and efficient alternative to detailed numerical simulations for fast and accurate prediction and control of coupled heat transfer in hollow concrete bricks.

the empirical transfer functions obtained by the two-step procedure described herein are very useful to predict the coupled heat transfer in hollow concrete bricks in time varying conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a simple and fast numerical procedure is proposed to predict heat transfer in vertically heated hollow bricks for a wide range of boundary conditions and material properties, which can be used for design and optimization purposes in a wide range of engineering applications.
the proposed procedure permits fast prediction of the coupled heat transfer in hollow concrete bricks in time varying conditions using simple transfer function models.
the empirical transfer functions are useful for predicting coupled heat transfer in vertically heated hollow bricks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the empirical transfer functions can be used to predict heat transfer for a wide variety of thermal excitations.

the empirical transfer functions coefficients can be generated for realistic thermal excitations and that they permit accurate predictions of coupled heat transfer in hollow concrete bricks in a wide range of realistic conditions.
the proposed numerical procedure can be used to obtain empirical TFCs for other types of coupled heat transfers in hollow concrete bricks.
